scene: one adult shopper stands at a plain shop counter holding a plain jacket on a hanger; on the counter opposite the jacket lies a very large pile of blank coins as payment, as tall as the jacket. The shopper looks at the pile with raised brows and a small tight mouth. The coins are blank discs with no numerals.
must: a very large pile of blank coins on the counter as payment.
avoid: a tiny pile of three coins (goedkoop); a man beside a box overflowing with coins (rijk); a heavy bag (zwaar); a big jacket (groot).
contrast: Pair with goedkoop. The only difference is the coin pile on the counter: very large here, three coins there.
example_nl: Een huis in de stad is duur.
example_en: A house in the city is expensive.
alt: Een vrouw houdt een jas vast; op de toonbank ligt een hoge stapel munten.

scene: one adult shopper stands at a plain shop counter holding a plain jacket on a hanger; on the counter opposite the jacket lie just three blank coins as payment. The shopper looks at them with a relaxed smile. The coins are blank discs with no numerals, and the wall behind is bare.
must: just three blank coins on the counter as payment.
avoid: a very large pile of coins (duur); a man with empty pockets and one coin (arm); a small jacket (klein); a shopper with empty hands (gratis).
contrast: Pair with duur. The only difference is the coin pile on the counter: three coins here, a very large pile there.
example_nl: Deze tas was heel goedkoop.
example_en: This bag was very cheap.
alt: Een vrouw houdt een jas vast; op de toonbank liggen drie munten.

scene: one adult sits on the edge of a plain bed with a lamp on the bedside table. The eyes are wide open, the brows high, the back straight and both feet on the floor, the lamp is lit with short rays.
must: wide open eyes and a straight back on the bed edge.
avoid: closed eyes and a slumped body (slaperig); a person lying under the blanket (slapen); a yawning mouth (slaperig); a person standing up (opstaan).
contrast: Pair with slaperig. The only difference is the face and posture: wide eyes and straight back here, half-closed eyes and a slump there.
example_nl: Ik ben al om zes uur wakker.
example_en: I am already awake at six o'clock.
alt: Een man zit rechtop op een bed; zijn ogen staan wijd open.

scene: one adult man sits on the edge of a plain bed with a lamp on the bedside table. The eyelids are half closed, the head droops to one side, the shoulders are slumped and the mouth is open in a big yawn with one hand in front of it.
must: half-closed eyes, a drooping head and a yawn.
avoid: wide open eyes and a straight back (wakker); a person lying asleep under a blanket (slapen); a sad downturned mouth (verdrietig); a man bent over panting after a run (moe).
contrast: Pair with wakker. The only difference is the face and posture: half-closed eyes, a yawn and a slump here, wide eyes and a straight back there.
example_nl: De baby is erg slaperig.
example_en: The baby is very sleepy.
alt: Een man zit op een bed met een hand voor zijn open mond; zijn ogen zijn half dicht.

scene: one adult stands next to a plain radio with a blank front and no numerals on a table; the radio has no sound lines at all. The adult has a calm face with the mouth closed, one finger lifted to the lips, and the hands are not at the ears.
must: a radio with no sound lines and a finger at closed lips.
avoid: a radio with many sound lines (luid); a person sleeping (slapen); a person with hands over the ears (luid); an empty room with no radio (leeg).
contrast: Pair with luid. The only difference is the radio: no sound lines here, many bold sound lines there.
example_nl: In de klas is het stil.
example_en: It is silent in the classroom.
alt: Een man staat naast een radio zonder lijnen en houdt een vinger bij zijn mond.

scene: one adult stands next to a plain radio with a blank front and no numerals on a table; five bold curved sound lines spread from the radio and the adult presses both hands flat over the ears, eyes squeezed shut, mouth pulled to the side.
must: five bold sound lines from the radio and hands over the ears.
avoid: a radio with no sound lines (stil); a person shouting with an open mouth (roepen); a person with a finger at the lips (stil); a drum or band (not the card).
contrast: Pair with stil. The only difference is the radio: five bold sound lines and hands over the ears here, no lines and a calm face there.
example_nl: De buurman lacht altijd heel luid.
example_en: The neighbour always laughs very loudly.
alt: Een man drukt zijn handen op zijn oren; uit de radio komen vijf lijnen.

scene: one adult man stands facing the viewer in a plain shirt with a visible patch on one elbow and a patch on the knee, the trouser pockets turned out and empty. The open box on the ground at his feet is empty, with one single blank coin beside it.
must: turned-out empty pockets and a single coin beside an empty box.
avoid: a person with a large coin pile (rijk); a thin tall person (dun); a person with an empty hand held open for nothing (leeg); a sad face alone (verdrietig).
contrast: Pair with rijk. The only difference is the wealth: empty pockets, patches and one coin here, a full coin box and fine clothes there.
example_nl: Die man is erg arm.
example_en: That man is very poor.
alt: Een man staat met lege zakken naast een lege doos met één munt.

scene: one adult man stands facing the viewer in a plain long coat with a plain hat, a ring on one finger. The open box on the ground at his feet overflows with a big heap of blank coins, a few coins spilling out onto the ground.
must: a box overflowing with coins at the man's feet.
avoid: a person with empty pockets and one coin (arm); a crown on the head (not the card); a big person (groot); a person holding a single coin (goedkoop).
contrast: Pair with arm. The only difference is the wealth: an overflowing coin chest and a fine coat here, empty pockets and one coin there.
example_nl: Mijn oom is heel rijk.
example_en: My uncle is very rich.
alt: Een man in een lange jas staat naast een doos vol munten.

scene: a wide plain square seen from slightly above with a single bench and a bare building front behind; only two adults stand far apart in the square, one sitting on the bench, with a lot of open empty ground between them.
must: only two people with wide open ground between them.
avoid: a crowded square (druk); a completely empty square (leeg); a person sleeping on the bench (slapen); a person sitting back with open hands and a soft smile (kalm).
contrast: Pair with druk. The only difference is the number of people: two here, about twenty there.
example_nl: Het park is vandaag rustig.
example_en: The park is quiet today.
alt: Op een groot plein zitten en staan twee mensen ver van elkaar.

scene: a wide plain square seen from slightly above with a single bench and a bare building front behind; about twenty adults fill the square, standing close together and overlapping, with almost no open ground between them.
must: about twenty people packed together across the whole square.
avoid: only two people spread out (rustig); a completely empty square (leeg); a few people standing in a line (rij); one person with a lot of tasks (not the card).
contrast: Pair with rustig. The only difference is the number of people: about twenty here, two there.
example_nl: De winkel is zaterdag heel druk.
example_en: The shop is very busy on Saturday.
alt: Een plein is vol mensen die dicht naast elkaar staan.

scene: one small child stands on flat grass at the left, side view, one adult a few steps behind, and one deep open hole in the ground just in front of the child. A plain wooden fence as high as the child's chest stands between the child and the hole. The adult stands still, looking at the child.
must: a fence standing between the child and the hole.
avoid: the same child and hole with no fence (gevaarlijk); a child crying (verdrietig); a child hiding behind the adult (bang); a fence round an empty field (not the card).
contrast: Pair with gevaarlijk. The only difference is the fence: it stands between the child and the hole here, it is missing there.
example_nl: Het kind is thuis veilig.
example_en: The child is safe at home.
alt: Een kind staat achter een hek; aan de andere kant van het hek is een diep gat.

scene: one small child stands on flat grass at the left, side view, one adult a few steps behind, and one deep open hole in the ground just in front of the child. Nothing stands between the child and the hole: the child's front foot is at the very edge. The adult stands still, looking at the child.
must: nothing between the child's feet and the deep hole.
avoid: the same child and hole with a fence between them (veilig); a child crying (verdrietig); a child hiding behind the adult (bang); a sharp knife on the ground (scherp).
contrast: Pair with veilig. The only difference is the fence: it is missing here, it stands between the child and the hole there.
example_nl: Deze drukke weg is gevaarlijk voor kinderen.
example_en: This busy road is dangerous for children.
alt: Een kind staat vlak bij de rand van een diep gat; er staat niets tussen het kind en het gat.

scene: a single plain flowerpot on a windowsill; the plant stands upright with a straight stem, many full leaves spread wide, and one open flower with petals. A small bee sits on the flower.
must: an upright plant with full leaves and an open flower.
avoid: a bent bare plant (dood); an empty pot (leeg); a cut flower in a vase (not the card); a painted flower (not the card).
contrast: Pair with dood. The only difference is the plant: upright with full leaves and a flower here, bent and bare there.
example_nl: Ik zie een levende vis in het water.
example_en: I see a living fish in the water.
alt: Een plant in een pot staat recht met veel bladeren en één open bloem.

scene: a single plain flowerpot on a windowsill; the plant has a thin stem bent sharply over the rim, only two curled leaves hang down and the flower head hangs bare and drooping. Cracked dry soil shows in the pot.
must: a bent bare stem with curled leaves over cracked soil.
avoid: an upright leafy plant (levend); an empty pot with no plant (leeg); a plant wrapped in cloth (not the card); a cut flower on a table (not the card).
contrast: Pair with levend. The only difference is the plant: bent and bare here, upright with full leaves and a flower there.
example_nl: De boom in onze tuin is dood.
example_en: The tree in our garden is dead.
alt: Een plant hangt kaal over de rand van een pot met droge, gebarsten grond.

scene: a row of three plain classroom desks with chairs, front view, a bare wall behind. An adult pupil sits at every desk, and the pupil at the middle desk raises one hand high, as if answering a name. No books, papers, numerals or writing anywhere.
must: the middle pupil sitting at the desk with a raised hand.
avoid: the same row with the middle seat empty (afwezig); a row of empty desks (leeg); a person walking out of the door (vertrekken); a pupil asleep at the desk (slapen).
contrast: Pair with afwezig. The only difference is the middle seat: a pupil sits there with a raised hand here, it stands empty there.
example_nl: Alle kinderen zijn vandaag aanwezig.
example_en: All the children are present today.
alt: Drie leerlingen zitten naast elkaar aan een tafeltje; de middelste steekt een hand op.

scene: a row of three plain classroom desks with chairs, front view, a bare wall behind. Adult pupils sit at the left and the right desk; the middle desk and its chair are empty, the chair pushed in. No books, papers, numerals or writing anywhere.
must: an empty middle seat between two seated pupils.
avoid: the same row with all three seats taken (aanwezig); a whole row of empty desks (leeg); a person walking out of the door (vertrekken); a pupil asleep at the desk (slapen).
contrast: Pair with aanwezig. The only difference is the middle seat: it stands empty here, a pupil sits there with a raised hand there.
example_nl: De leraar is vandaag afwezig.
example_en: The teacher is absent today.
alt: Twee leerlingen zitten links en rechts aan een tafeltje; de stoel in het midden is leeg.

scene: one adult stands facing the viewer in a plain shirt that hangs wide and baggy, the sleeves covering the hands and large folds hanging from the chest; air gaps are drawn clearly between the cloth and the body at both sides.
must: a wide baggy shirt with clear air gaps at the sides.
avoid: a shirt pressed to the body (strak); a big adult (groot); a shirt lying on the ground (not the card); a shirt coming off the body (uittrekken).
contrast: Pair with strak. The only difference is the shirt: wide with air gaps here, pressed to the body there.
example_nl: Deze broek is te wijd.
example_en: These trousers are too loose.
alt: Een man draagt een shirt met veel ruimte tussen de stof en zijn lichaam.

scene: one adult stands facing the viewer in a plain shirt that is pulled tight across the chest and stomach; small tension lines pull at the seams and buttons, and the cloth follows the body outline closely with no air gap.
must: a shirt pulled tight with tension lines at the seams.
avoid: a wide baggy shirt (wijd); a thin adult (dun); a belt tied tight on the waist only (not the card); a fat adult (dik).
contrast: Pair with wijd. The only difference is the shirt: pressed to the body with tension lines here, wide with air gaps there.
example_nl: Dit shirt zit te strak.
example_en: This shirt is too tight.
alt: Een man draagt een shirt dat nauw om zijn borst zit met kleine trekstrepen.

scene: one adult man stands on a plain park path just after a run, side view, bent forward with both hands on the knees, head hanging, mouth open and panting, and sweat drops flying from the forehead. He does not yawn. A single bare tree stands behind.
must: a man bent over with hands on the knees and sweat drops.
avoid: an upright man with loose arms and a smile (fit); a yawning man with half-closed eyes (slaperig); a person sleeping in bed (slapen); a sad face with tears (verdrietig); a person bent under a heavy box (zwaar).
contrast: Pair with fit. The only difference is the posture: bent over with hands on the knees and sweat drops here, upright with loose arms and a smile there.
example_nl: Na het werk ben ik moe.
example_en: After work I am tired.
alt: Een man staat voorovergebogen met zijn handen op zijn knieën; er vliegen zweetdruppels van zijn voorhoofd.

scene: the same adult man stands on the plain park path just after a run, side view, upright with an open chest, arms hanging loose, both feet on the ground, breathing calmly with a smile. No sweat drops and no speed lines. A single bare tree stands behind.
must: an upright man standing easily with loose arms and a smile.
avoid: a man bent over with hands on the knees (moe); a bodybuilder with huge muscles (sterk); a person running fast with speed lines (snel); a person sleeping (slapen).
contrast: Pair with moe. The only difference is the posture: upright with loose arms and a smile here, bent over with hands on the knees and sweat drops there.
example_nl: Mijn opa is nog erg fit.
example_en: My grandfather is still very fit.
alt: Een man staat rechtop op een pad met ontspannen armen en lacht.

scene: one child stands facing a plain big dog on a plain street; the child leans the whole body back away from the dog, both hands pressed against the chest, brows raised and tilted, eyes wide and the mouth open, and one foot steps back.
must: a child leaning back with raised brows and hands at the chest facing a dog.
avoid: a child stepping toward the dog with a smile (dapper); a child crying alone (verdrietig); a child with clenched fists and raised shoulders (gespannen); a child wringing the hands and tapping a foot (zenuwachtig).
contrast: Pair with dapper. The only difference is the child: leaning back with raised brows here, standing tall and stepping forward there.
example_nl: Ik ben bang voor de hond.
example_en: I am afraid of the dog.
alt: Een kind leunt achteruit voor een grote hond met wijd open ogen.

scene: one child stands facing a plain big dog on a plain street; the child stands tall with the chest out, chin lifted, brows level and firm, a small smile, and one foot steps forward with a hand held out toward the dog.
must: a child standing tall and stepping toward a dog with a firm brow.
avoid: a child leaning back with wide eyes (bang); a child running away (rennen); a child hugging the dog (not the card); a big muscular child (sterk).
contrast: Pair with bang. The only difference is the child: standing tall and stepping forward here, leaning back with raised brows there.
example_nl: De kleine jongen is erg dapper.
example_en: The little boy is very brave.
alt: Een kind staat rechtop en steekt een hand uit naar een grote hond.

scene: the same two children at a plain table, front view, upper bodies, one plain round cake with no candles on a plate between them. One straight cut line runs exactly through the middle of the cake, making two halves of the same size, and each child points a fork at the half nearest to them. Both faces are calm.
must: the cut line exactly through the middle, two halves of the same size.
avoid: the cake cut well off the middle into a big and a small piece (oneerlijk); one whole cake with no cut (heel); one big cake next to one small cake (groot); two adults breaking a loaf between them (not the card); a cake with candles and garlands (feestelijk).
contrast: Pair with oneerlijk. The only difference is the cut line: through the middle with two equal halves here, well off the middle with one big and one small piece there.
example_nl: Iedereen krijgt evenveel, dat is eerlijk.
example_en: Everyone gets the same amount, that is fair.
alt: Twee kinderen zitten aan tafel met een taart die precies door het midden in twee even grote stukken is gesneden.

scene: the same two children at a plain table, front view, upper bodies, one plain round cake with no candles on a plate between them. One straight cut line runs well to one side of the middle, making one big piece and one small piece; the child on the left points a fork at the big piece, the child on the right at the small piece. Both faces are calm.
must: the cut line well off the middle, one big piece and one small piece.
avoid: the cake cut through the middle into two equal halves (eerlijk); one big cake next to one small cake (groot); a boy clutching a bag of sweets away from a girl (gierig); a child with an empty plate (leeg); a child crying with drooping brows (verdrietig).
contrast: Pair with eerlijk. The only difference is the cut line: well off the middle with one big and one small piece here, through the middle with two equal halves there.
example_nl: Hij krijgt meer dan ik, dat is oneerlijk.
example_en: He gets more than me, that is unfair.
alt: Twee kinderen zitten aan tafel met een taart die ver naast het midden is gesneden, in een groot en een klein stuk.
